content:
For more than 30 years, the Cruz family has sold antojitos at Nuevo Laredo's fiestas patronales, according to El Mañana de Nuevo Laredo. The family's food stand has become part of the rhythm of the city's patron saint festivals, where neighbors gather, eat, and celebrate year after year.

Fiestas patronales are community celebrations built around a town's patron saint, and their food stalls are often family operations passed down through generations. Three decades at those festivals means the Cruz family's antojitos have fed parents and, later, their children at the same gatherings.

It is the kind of quiet, steady presence that holds a community celebration together: the same family, the same stand, returning for the fiestas season after season.

Sources:

  • El Mañana de Nuevo Laredo, "Familia Cruz suma más de 30 años vendiendo antojitos en las fiestas patronales de Nuevo Laredo," Oct. 27, 2026
